transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-05-19
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Kaur (Sentinel Head of Security), Tomás Rivera (Platform Eng), Nicole Park (CTO)

Auto-generated Topics (may be imperfect):
- hosting options: hosted, dedicated, private
- compliance: SOC 2, ISO27001, data residency
- identity: SSO / SAML / SCIM, RBAC
- key management: KMS passthrough, HSM, envelope encryption
- logging and retention: audit logs, retention window, export

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. we're Maya from Redwood, AE, with Diego our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to talk through security and hosting options.
[00:14] Nicole: Hi all, Nicole here. We're mostly trying to map out gating criteria for infra and security before we commit to a POC.
[00:21] Maya: Totally. Quick agenda — we'll confirm requirements, run through our hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, focus on identity and keys, and wrap with next steps.
[00:30] Tomás: Sounds good. We're particularly interested in KMS passthrough and how audit logs are surfaced.

[02:12] Diego: Quick note — when we say KMS passthrough we mean customers can bring their own cloud KMS and we avoid unwrapping keys on our control plane. there are different patterns: CSP KMS integration, HSM-backed on-prem, or envelope with customer keys.
[02:33] Aisha: Can you summarize which options are available for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? I want the legal team to see the differences.
[02:40] Maya: Yes. Hosted: fastest, we manage keys by default but you can opt for customer-managed KMS with limited passthrough on Dedicated and Private. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation and KMS passthrough via IAM role trust. Private: VPC or on-prem where customer retains full key control and network isolation.
[03:05] Nicole: When you say "limited passthrough" what's limited?
[03:12] Diego: Good question. The limitation is around direct HSM access from our runtime in Hosted. For Hosted we don't allow raw HSM pins into our shared control plane for security reasons; instead we use envelope encryption where the DEK is wrapped by customer KMS. For Dedicated you can set up a private endpoint and IAM roles so the runtime talks to your KMS in your account. Private gives you full control — it's packaged for air-gapped or on-prem.

[05:00] Aisha: We're SOC 2 in process; legal needs the Type II before procurement. Do you have a Type II?
[05:07] Maya: We do. We can share the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 attestation. I'll drop them to the channel.
[05:15] Aisha: Great. Also our SSO is SAML-based through Okta; we need SCIM provisioning and RBAC that maps to our groups.
[05:25] Diego: Redwood supports SAML and OIDC. SCIM for user provisioning is available on Dedicated and Private by default; for Hosted we support SCIM for orgs on enterprise plans. RBAC is role-based with custom roles and token scopes.
[06:02] Tomás: Are tokens per-user or per-service? We have service accounts that call the API from backend services.
[06:09] Maya: You can do both. We issue API keys and short-lived tokens via the SSO flow. For service accounts you can create machine identities and pin scopes.

[08:10] Nicole: Audit logging — what level of detail? Who can access logs, and how long do you retain them?
[08:18] Diego: We capture request/response-level traces for ops (sanitized), authentication events, admin actions like role changes, and model rollouts. For Hosted default retention is 90 days; Dedicated and Private can extend — we often push logs to customer-managed S3 or SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) for long-term retention.
[08:45] Aisha: Legal wants 12 months retention for audit trails, plus attestations that logs are tamper-evident. Can Redwood export logs to our S3 with KMS encryption?
[08:58] Maya: Yes, we can stream logs to your S3 bucket using cross-account IAM role; objects can be encrypted with your KMS. That's a common pattern for Dedicated and Private.

[11:20] Tomás: On performance — if we do Dedicated with KMS calls per request for envelope decryption, does that add latency? We're sensitive to p95 latency at sub-200ms for short chats.
[11:32] Diego: KMS round-trips can add tens to low hundreds of milliseconds depending on region. We recommend caching DEKs in the runtime KV cache to avoid per-token KMS hops; pattern is: unwrap short-lived DEK at request start and reuse for session chunking. We'll show benchmarks in the POC.
[12:05] Tomás: OK that matches our internal thinking. We'll want to validate with a traffic sample.

[14:40] Aisha: On SSO provisioning, we need group mapping so that when someone leaves our org they lose access immediately. How is revocation handled?
[14:50] Diego: Revocation happens centrally via identity provider — SCIM deprovisioning removes the user; we also honor SAML session logout. Additionally tokens respect short TTLs and we support an administrative "revoke key" action that invalidates existing API keys.
[15:10] Aisha: Is there an audit trail for revocations?
[15:14] Maya: Yes, admin actions are logged with actor and timestamp and can be exported.

[18:00] Nicole: Data residency — some of our customers require EU-only storage for specific datasets. Does Redwood allow per-tenant region pinning?
[18:10] Maya: We support region pinning for models and storage for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has region options but doesn't guarantee per-tenant physical separation unless on an enterprise contract with regional isolation add-on.
[18:28] Nicole: So for EU-only requirements Dedicated in EU region or Private in our EU cloud would be the route.
[18:34] Maya: Correct.

[21:05] Tomás: Encryption in transit and at rest — are TLS and AES-256 standard? Any FIPS requirements?
[21:12] Diego: TLS 1.2+/1.3 in transit; at-rest AES-256 with KMS wrapping. For FIPS we have guidance for Private where customers can use FIPS-validated modules in their environment. For Hosted, we do not claim FIPS compliance out-of-the-box.

[24:40] Aisha: On access controls — does Redwood do attribute-based access? We want to map product roles to Okta groups and add extra policy gates for data access.
[24:52] Diego: We currently support RBAC with custom roles and attribute checks in Dedicated/Private. We can enforce group-based access and posture gating at the request layer — e.g., prevent exports for certain roles. Full ABAC is roadmap but we can implement policy hooks for customers in POCs.

[27:30] Nicole: Our procurement will ask about incident response and breach notifications. What's SLAs and notification timeline?
[27:38] Maya: SLA varies by plan. For Dedicated we offer uptimes and a 1-hour response for Sev1. For Hosted it's lower. We have an incident runbook and notify customers within 72 hours for confirmed data exposures, and we provide forensic artifacts under NDA.
[28:05] Aisha: 72 hours is fine as a baseline; legal will ask for guaranteed timelines in the contract.

[30:00] Tomás: Can we get a network diagram of your deployment and control plane flows? We need to show our network/security folks how DNS, NAT, and KMS calls flow.
[30:08] Diego: Absolutely. I'll draft a diagram showing control plane vs data plane, KMS endpoints, and recommended Private VPC peering.

[32:50] Maya: Quick question on retention: you mentioned 12 months for logs. What about model input retention? Are you allowed to instruct Redwood to not persist prompts?
[33:00] Aisha: For certain PII or regulated PII we want a no-persist option or redaction prior to storage.
[33:10] Diego: We offer data controls. For Hosted we have request-level flags to opt out of retention for specific calls; Dedicated and Private give customers the choice to disable persistence entirely. We also provide a redaction webhook to scrub PII before storage.

[36:20] Nicole: For the POC, we'd like to validate: latency with KMS passthrough, SCIM provisioning flows, and that audit logs can be exported to our SIEM with your object naming scheme.
[36:30] Maya: Good checklist. We'll propose a two-week POC with those three validations.

[38:40] Tomás: Any lock-in concerns? If we build with Redwood Dedicated, how portable are our prompts and model choices?
[38:48] Diego: The API is standard REST/SDK, models are pulled from a catalog; you can pin model versions. For portability we support export of prompts and evaluation artifacts. You'd still need to migrate model binaries if you move away from Redwood.

[41:00] Aisha: A couple of quick compliance asks: will you provide SOC2 control mappings to our control framework and a list of subprocessors?
[41:09] Maya: Yes, SOC2 mapping and subprocessor list are part of our standard security packet. We'll include the current list and update cadence.

[43:23] Diego: One minor gotcha I want to flag — if you enable very short-lived DEKs and you have a high throughput burst, KMS throttling could surface as increased latency. Our recommended mitigation is a small DEK cache with rekey frequency tuned to session length. We'll include tuning guidance.
[43:45] Tomás: Good to know, we'll want to include that in the POC scope.

[45:00] Maya: Recap and next steps: I'll send SOC2 and ISO docs, schedule the POC (two-week dedicated setup), Diego will send VPC topology and RBAC patterns, Tomás will share traffic sample, Aisha will confirm retention policy and legal must-haves.
[45:18] Nicole: Sounds good. Can we schedule the kickoff next Tuesday at 15:00?
[45:25] Maya: I'll propose it in the calendar.
[45:28] Aisha: Thanks, talk soon.
[45:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, bye.

Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript quality: some technical terms may be mis-transcribed (SAML sometimes shown as 'sam-el', KMS as 'K M S'); timestamps approximate.
